back: Elimination: zero cases in a defined area with continuing action. Eradication: permanent zero cases worldwide, so control is no longer needed.
Island country; borders closed from 19 March 2020; Level 4 lockdown from 25 March 2020; elimination strategy until late 2021; wage subsidy; high public trust.
First case 20 March 2020; lockdown from 30 March 2020; limited testing and support; large informal economy; vaccination from February 2021 with donated doses.
Geography (island or land borders), wealth and health systems, informal economy, governance and trust, access to vaccines.

Launched in 1988; cases down by over 99% from an estimated 350 000 in 125 countries; wild types 2 (2015) and 3 (2019) eradicated; Africa certified free of wild polio in 2020; wild type 1 remains in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

front: Why polio is hard to eradicate
back: Silent infections, conflict and insecurity, distrust of campaigns, weak routine immunisation, population movement, and vaccine-derived strains from the live oral vaccine.
No animal reservoir, clear visible symptoms, an effective stable vaccine with lasting immunity; declared eradicated in 1980.
Threshold = 1 − 1/R₀; for R₀ = 6 it is about 83%.
